name: Mariah Carey
notes: The belt-ballad blueprint for the whole lane. The research pairs 54–86 with a half-time feel, the backbeat on 3 and a 16th-note subdivision, so `halfTime` is true and the snare is `halftime_3`; the 96–128 uptempo band is the straight-time wing and is named here rather than encoded. The hip-hop-soul half of the catalogue "sits on a sampled break with a swung 16th grid", which is the one warrant for moving `swing` off straight — 0.54 on a 16th grid, the subtle modern R&B setting. Three drum deltas are quoted: "a gated/roomy snare on 3", "kick 1 and 3", and "a 16th hi-hat or shaker", which is the shaker-led perc block. Harmony is the entry's richest claim — flat-side majors with "maj7, add9, ii–V–I turnarounds and gospel-derived IV/vi–IV plagal cadences" — so the triad share drops to 0.36 with sevenths and ninths carrying the rest, and ii–V–I and IV–I are authored families. The melody is written from the entry's own division of labour: "chorus melody is stepwise and singable while the ad-libs above it carry the virtuosity", so the lead is stepwise and low-density and the countermelody sits an octave above at a high ratio, which is where the melisma lives. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium and says voicing detail is partly convention-derived. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are the drum probabilities, `swing.amount` 0.54 and `bpm.mode` 68. ⚠ **`bassline.rhythm` is `independent_riff`, not `reese_sustain`** — the research names two low ends and the model could only encode one: *“sustained synth or played bass on roots and inversions under the ballads; sample-derived sub on the uptempos, following the loop rather than the kick”*. *Following the loop rather than the kick* is `independent_riff` by definition — the engine's one rhythm that places its own onsets — and it is the mode the entry gives a figure to. The sustained ballad reading is what the high `followRootsProb` keeps.
